sources.source_name: Home Depot Product Listing - Glacier Bay VT3322A08
sources.snippet: All-in-One 33" x 22" drop-in double bowl. 22-gauge stainless steel. Includes faucet, drain assemblies, and basket strainers. Drop-in/self-rimming installation. 8" basin depth. T-304 stainless claimed. 1-year limited warranty. Price: ~$119-149. No sound deadening pads mentioned in product specifications.
sources.classification_reason: Product listing with spec data — 22-gauge and 1-year warranty are scoring inputs.

sources.snippet: Glacier Bay is builder-grade filler. The 22-gauge stainless flexes if you push on it. No sound deadening whatsoever — drops a fork and the whole kitchen hears it. The included faucet is garbage. I've pulled these out of new construction that's under 2 years old — they dent, they flex at the mounting clips, and the drain baskets corrode. If you can afford $50 more, get literally anything else.
sources.classification_reason: Professional plumber direct experience with specific failure modes documented.

sources.snippet: Replaced a Glacier Bay that came with our builder-grade new construction. After 3 years: dented bottom bowl, water spots that wouldn't come off (looked like permanent staining), constant 'tinny' noise from dishes. The drop-in rim collects grime. Upgraded to a Kraus 16-gauge undermount — night and day difference in feel, sound, and quality.
sources.classification_reason: Consumer long-term experience with specific durability failures.

sources.snippet: In the budget tier, Glacier Bay is at the absolute floor. Dayton by Elkay is a step up (still budget, but better gauge and sound dampening). The jump from 22-gauge to 18-gauge is massive — it's the difference between a sink that flexes and a sink that holds solid. Glacier Bay's 1-year warranty vs lifetime warranties from established brands tells you everything about manufacturer confidence.
sources.classification_reason: Professional plumber comparative hierarchy with specific construction analysis.

sources.source_name: Home Depot Brand Research - Glacier Bay OEM
sources.snippet: Glacier Bay is Home Depot's exclusive private-label brand. Products are manufactured by various OEMs — suspected Globe Union/Foremost for sinks and faucets. Home Depot does not manufacture any products. No plumbing supply house distribution. No professional installer endorsement. Positioned as entry-level/builder-grade.

bottom_line: Glacier Bay VT3322A08 is the builder-grade floor of the residential sink market. 22-gauge stainless steel is the thinnest commonly sold — flexes under normal use, resonates noise with every dish contact, and dents from routine pot/pan handling. No sound deadening of any kind. Drop-in installation is the simplest, least premium mounting. Unknown OEM manufacturing (likely Globe Union/Foremost under Home Depot private label). 1-year warranty vs lifetime from every established competitor signals zero manufacturer confidence. Professional plumber consensus: 'absolute floor — most callbacks, most replacements.' The included faucet is disposable-grade. Only bright spot: universal drain parts compatibility. Expected lifespan under 15 years with normal kitchen use. Price-point ($119-149) explains everything.
